sources.title: Indigenous knowledge systems and their implications for sustainable development in Zimbabwe
sources.author: Mapira, J. and Mazambara, P.
sources.note: Journal of Sustainable Development in Africa 15(5), 90 to 106. Table 3 lists common totems in Zimbabwe.

sources.title: How our totems came about, purposes
sources.author: Gracious Mugovera (Manica Post), citing Prof. Isheunesu Mpepereki and historians
sources.note: Notes that Ndebele izibongo often come from ancestors’ names rather than animals.

sources.title: Totems as identity and inheritance: what is in your mutupo?
sources.author: The Herald
sources.note: Background source named in the brief.

sources.title: Kwaunobva: mitupo pages
sources.author: Kwaunobva
sources.note: Per-totem pages with praise names for men and women, regions and praise poem openings.

sources.title: Soko (Tsoko) mutupo
sources.author: Chivara
sources.note: Identifies Soko as the vervet monkey.

sources.title: Mutupo: 6 interesting things you should know about Shona totems, praise names and poetry
sources.author: ZimbOriginal
sources.note: Table of mitupo and zvidawo; says Dziva has three totem animals (hungwe, mvuu, hove).

sources.title: Mutupo survey: insights from over 1,000 people
sources.author: ZimbOriginal
sources.note: Soko respondents mostly named the vervet monkey, a few the baboon. Same animal can be shared by unrelated clans.

sources.title: Shava Totem
sources.author: Wikipedia
sources.note: Shava is a variant of Mhofu/Mpofu (eland); Kalanga use Mpofu. Article flagged as needing citations.

sources.title: Kalanga people
sources.author: Wikipedia
sources.note: Mndambeli clan venerates Ghudo (baboon) or Tembo; others use Shoko, Zhou and Tshuma.

sources.title: Venda people
sources.author: Wikipedia
sources.note: Names the Ndou clan and the Vha Ha-Maḓavha (warthogs) who came from Zimbabwe. Does not discuss totems directly.

sources.title: Sibanda
sources.author: Wikipedia
sources.note: Lion totem; common among Ndebele and Sotho families in Zimbabwe.

sources.title: Ndlovu
sources.author: Wikipedia
sources.note: Ndlovu means elephant; common among Ndebele and Zulu people.

sources.title: Clans and totems in Ndebele culture
sources.author: BeingAfrican
sources.note: Lists 15 Ndebele clans (izibongo) with totems (isitemo).

sources.title: Zimbabwean totems and what they mean
sources.author: Zimbabwe Profiles
sources.note: Broad list with praise names. Contains unsourced claims about character traits, which are not used.

sources.title: Shona totems (mitupo): how animal symbols shape identity and guide marriage
sources.author: Nkenne
sources.note: Totem meanings and taboos; mentions Kamba (tortoise) and Dziva as water.

sources.title: The Mbada (leopard) totem
sources.author: Zvangu
sources.note: Links Mbada (leopard) to the Nhewa and Simboti clans.

sources.title: Ncube / Soko totem: what they represent
sources.author: Totem Network blog
sources.note: Soko as monkey/baboon; explains Mukanya as the galloping steps of a baboon climbing a mountain.

sources.title: History of the VaNambya people of Hwange District
sources.author: Zimtribes
sources.note: Hwange dynasty founder of the Soko (monkey) totem; dynasty earlier Moyo.

sources.title: Tonga groups (reader comments)
sources.author: Zimtribes
sources.note: Clan and totem pairs come only from reader comments and some contradict each other. Low reliability.
